prompt: Many people say that globalisation and the growing number of multinational companies have a negative effect on the environment. To what extent do you agree or disagree? Use specific reasons and examples to support your position.
essay:
Globalisation has transformed the world by promoting international trade, investment, and economic growth. At the same time, the rapid expansion of multinational corporations has enabled businesses to operate on an unprecedented global scale. While these developments have undoubtedly brought significant economic benefits, I strongly agree that they have also had a largely detrimental impact on the environment due to increased industrial activity and excessive consumption.

One of the primary reasons for this environmental damage is the growth of large-scale manufacturing. To meet the ever-increasing global demand for goods, multinational companies establish factories in various countries, many of which rely heavily on fossil fuels. As a result, vast amounts of greenhouse gases and industrial waste are released into the atmosphere and nearby water bodies, contributing to climate change and environmental pollution. For example, many manufacturing hubs in developing countries have experienced severe air and water pollution because environmental regulations are often less strictly enforced than in developed nations.

Another major concern is the expansion of international transportation networks. Globalisation has created complex supply chains in which raw materials, components, and finished products are transported across continents by ships, trucks, and aircraft. These modes of transport consume enormous quantities of fuel and generate substantial carbon emissions. Moreover, multinational corporations often encourage a culture of mass consumption through aggressive advertising and frequent product launches. This leads consumers to replace perfectly usable products with newer versions, resulting in excessive waste, greater pressure on natural resources, and growing landfill sites.

Admittedly, some multinational companies have begun investing in renewable energy, environmentally friendly packaging, and sustainable production methods. However, these initiatives remain insufficient to offset the environmental costs associated with large-scale production and global distribution.

In conclusion, although globalisation has accelerated economic development and improved living standards in many parts of the world, I firmly believe that its environmental consequences are overwhelmingly negative. Unless governments and multinational corporations adopt more sustainable practices, environmental degradation is likely to become an even greater global challenge in the future.
